newsitem.title: UK: London platinum fixes at 40-month low.
newsitem.headline: London platinum fixes at 40-month low.

text.p: Platinum fell to its lowest fixing since September 15, 1993 on Thursday when it was fixed at $355.85 per ounce.
The low on September 15, 1993 was $353.00. This morning platinum fixed at $356.25 matching the fresh low since October 5,1993 set on Tuesday.
Dealers said platinum was attracting very little interest despite its low price.
"It has been caught in the downdraft from gold and has virtually no life of its own," a dealer said.
Japan is the largest user of the blue-white metal which is used in jewellery, autocatalysts and a variety of chemical and electronic applications.
It is chiefly mined in South Africa and Russia and a recent report from leading refiner Johnson Matthey suggested the market would be fully supplied this year.
